requirements.requirement: Bundled limactl with the virtualization entitlement boots a VZ guest from inside the sandboxed backend subtree, without QEMU
requirements.caveat: Lima's own ad hoc signature was used. Re-signing with Developer ID and hardened runtime belongs to the release pipeline (delivery step 3) and must be rechecked there. An ad hoc probe signed with --options runtime and the same entitlement also started a VZ VM from the sandbox.

requirements.requirement: Host GUI probes stay denied while Lima's host processes run
requirements.note: Probes ran from the sandboxed shell whose descendants are limactl and its host agent; the sandbox is inherited, and ps is denied there, so the host agent itself was not probed directly. The VZ VM process is Apple's XPC service, launched outside the sandbox by design.

requirements.requirement: A virtiofs export mounts at its canonical path
As a non-sudo f5 user, bubblewrap and socat let the Claude CLI sandbox enforce a child sandbox
requirements.caveat: Verified with sandbox-runtime (the library the Claude CLI's sandbox uses) via srt, not with the Claude CLI driving a model; the provider test against a fake model server remains in the test plan.

requirements.requirement: Root-owned nftables block the host gateway, RFC1918, link-local and CGNAT while DNS and public egress work
requirements.note: Host gateway, LAN router and CGNAT were reachable without the policy and blocked with it. Link-local had no responder either way, so it is covered only by the rule.

requirements.requirement: The limactl shell stdio channel carries frames; stdin EOF stops the backend's systemd scope
requirements.note: Used F5's merged streamBackendChannel. A 1 MiB frame echoed; a detached grandchild in its own session died with the scope while the backend ignored EOF.

requirements.requirement: A main-owned ssh ControlMaster adds and cancels 127.0.0.1 forwards at runtime under the sandbox
Cold-boot time and resident memory recorded

supersededChecks.reason: Probe defect: it tested the network with getent, which resolves through systemd-resolved's UNIX socket even with the network namespace unshared. b:sandbox.bwrap_unprivileged reran it with a TCP connection to an IP address: NONET.

ripgrep was missing from the spike guest. Rerun in Phase B after installing it. A first Phase B run passed wrongly (srt was given the command as one argv and the check matched text inside its error), so that run was discarded; the recorded Phase B run uses srt -c and exact matching.

designFindings: virtiofs maps every guest write to the host user (502:20) whatever the guest uid, so guest users do not protect exported files. Exports must be treated as fully guest-writable, as the plan already says.

A bubblewrap sandbox that binds / still reaches guest UNIX sockets: DNS resolved through systemd-resolved's socket with the network namespace unshared. Child-sandbox policy must hide sockets such as /run/systemd and the D-Bus bus.
sandbox-runtime refuses to run without ripgrep; the guest image must keep it.
The guest's DNS server is the gateway (192.168.5.2:53 via gvproxy), so the policy needs its narrow DNS exception on the host gateway.
Idle host RSS is about 0.7 GiB per VM with 4 GiB configured; that supports the cap of two running VMs.
Lima's host agent already keeps its own persistent ControlMaster; a separate main-owned master with its own ControlPath coexisted with it.
First boot with apt provisioning took 84 s; the prebuilt image removes that. Cold boots of a provisioned guest took 6.5 to 9.8 s.

In one Phase B run the limactl shell process exited 241 after main closed the channel, though the scope had been stopped; the rerun exited 0. The VM launcher should judge success by the scope, not by that exit code.
